newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL one-week interbank rate eases on maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL one-week interbank rate eases on maturity.

text.p: The one-week interbank rate eased to 6.50/80 percent against 7.10/20 previously after the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill, dealers said on Friday.
They said banks were preferring to keep their funds in shorter tenures ahead of a two billion ringgit 10-year government bond issue on November 29.
Two-week money declined to 7.10/20 percent against 7.25/35 on Thursday.
The dealers said the maturity would also keep the overnight rate for the weekend unchanged at 6.00 percent.
They said most other interbank rates were unchanged from their previous levels.
One-month money was at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.30/35.
"People want to set aside funds for the bond issue," a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur said.
He said while the overnight rate will remain depressed until next week, longer-term rates may go up for want of funds.
Liquidity would improve further after a Bank Negara deposit, borrowed as part of its open market intervention, matures next Monday.
Dealers said a mismatch in fund flows arising from the issue would keep the rates volatile for two to three weeks.
The issue is to be partially offset by two bond maturities totalling 1.1 billion ringgit, but they would mature only on December 15.
